feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain depth, steady progression, and relevant technical breadth. It reads professionally and is rich in scope, but impact is diluted by repetition, limited outcome-focused metrics beyond one role, and a slightly overloaded structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary immediately establish a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and public-sector communications.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with visible advancement from coordinator to director to consultant signals trust and leadership growth.  
- Good specificity: strong tools/platform detail (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, AI search, multimedia) makes the profile concrete and modern.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve scannability and avoid keyword stuffing.  
- Add more measurable outcomes across roles: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results would strengthen impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, campaign performance).  
- Tighten writing consistency: there are minor stylistic inconsistencies such as “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” alongside less hyphenated compounds, and mixed list punctuation. No major misspellings or grammar errors found, but standardize commas in series (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other lists) and date style (“Oct.”/“Sept.”/“Mar.”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and foregrounding the most distinctive value will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a sharper version: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Combines strategic leadership with hands-on delivery across Drupal platforms, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and user experiences.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling” for stronger executive tone.
- Add one concrete differentiator if space allows, such as “high-volume” or “enterprise” web environments, to reinforce scale.
- Use parallel phrasing in the second sentence; the current list is strong but reads long.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with footer project content and core competencies; “AI-enabled search” would be more specific.
- “Governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and competencies section.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized distinctive capability areas and used tighter, more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, category-style wording: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership
- Tighten technical/innovation items: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations
- Clarify sector/value focus: Public-sector advocacy communications
- Refine production line for consistency: Multimedia production, livestreaming and studio operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already prominent in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps with multiple work experience bullets; consider “cross-channel communications leadership” to sound more senior and less repetitive.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise achievement-focused bullet for easier scanning.
- Use parallel verbs and cleaner phrasing: “Created AI-enabled legislative search using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat.”
- Replace vague wording like “designed for continued campaign growth” with more specific value, e.g., “built for reuse and future campaign expansion.”
- Standardize style: use “10 x 20-foot” (not 10×20-foot) and keep punctuation consistent across all project entries.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite substantially overlap with the current consultant role; keep these shorter here to avoid repeating Work Experience.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with multiple NACo roles; consider emphasizing what was distinctive about the series or removing it if space is tight.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with prior NACo entries and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consulting-level impact, platform outcomes, and what is new since the director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused lines, e.g.:
- “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved cross-channel communications operations by refining workflows, governance, analytics, and publishing systems across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, publishing efficiency gains, search relevance improvements, or campaign engagement metrics.
- Replace generic phrases like “deliver technical troubleshooting” with stronger verbs: “implemented,” “optimized,” “stabilized,” “streamlined.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” and “enterprise web improvement” repeat the 2022–2024 director role unless tied to new consulting outcomes.
- Microsites/AI search duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for the project section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be stronger if tightened around 3–4 signature outcomes and phrased to emphasize transformation, team leadership, and business impact over channel inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and multi-channel communications for a national membership organization.”
- Combine the website bullets and keep the strongest metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership outcome-oriented: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with a result such as audience growth, engagement, send volume, or campaign performance if available.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting and decision-making” and “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to streamline digital operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video-program growth overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on building the in-house studio and enterprise-scale leadership.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears in the current consultant role; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, channel ownership, and concrete scale so it shows clear growth into the Director role.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Combine related bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders, supporting consistent policy and member communications.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable channel for policy communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct contribution: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet; keep this version more execution-focused.
- The advocacy video point also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project; avoid repeating “first” or broad video-program claims here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and emphasize senior leadership scope rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance and editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector digital communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider changing the title to “Digital Strategy, Governance & Content Operations” to better match the experience.
- Drop “messaging” unless you want to foreground brand/policy communications; your experience reads more as systems, operations, and platform leadership.
- If space allows, add one scale cue in the title line or nearby section instead of here (e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “50+ publishers”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker than the more concrete planning/operations language used in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first; they are most supported by recent experience and strongest differentiators.
- Remove weaker/older-feeling standalone tool mentions unless they support target roles; “WordPress” may be kept, but de-emphasized after Drupal/modernization.
- If space allows, sharpen outcomes-oriented language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “AI-enabled search and discovery” reads stronger than generic “technical execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the technical section carry the full tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic analytics leadership, not repeat software names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than a pure platform list.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO and performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: “KPI and dashboard design” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting.”
- Optional rewrite: “Analytics strategy • KPI and dashboard design • Executive reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Technical + IT” analytics section almost exactly; keep detailed tools there and make this version more strategic.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact framing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more senior and distinctive by emphasizing production leadership and delivery environments rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-/scope-oriented skills, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the Director-level studio work.
- Replace “Hybrid and virtual event production” with “Livestream and hybrid event production” for tighter phrasing and less repetition.
- If space allows, consider “Studio systems and live production operations” to sound more strategic than “Studio operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- This section should not restate older hands-on duties if recent leadership bullets already cover studio buildout and multimedia expansion.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s redundant with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills and misses a chance to signal depth in the most relevant platform. Since recent experience is heavily Drupal-led, that should be emphasized.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light proficiency framing if space allows: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If you want more impact, replace the flat list with: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites and modular content), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep this item platform-only; leave implementation details to the coding/technical section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills > “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Consider trimming one section or using this item for platform names only and the Topline Skills entry for broader capabilities.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” should stay out of this item to avoid overlap.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools that support recent delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in current work; if kept, place it last to signal legacy familiarity rather than core strength.
- If space allows, add one specificity cue tied to recent work, e.g. **front-end CMS implementation**, **deployment automation**, or **serverless scripting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place.
- **Google Tag Manager** may fit better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** unless you want this section strictly implementation-oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize systems ownership, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**.
- Tighten to the most relevant, differentiated tools: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**.
- Drop lower-signal or older/general tools unless central to recent work: **Basecamp, Trello**.
- If format allows, add light grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/ops:** Jira, Asana | **Collaboration:** Slack, Teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- **Airtable** and **workflow automation** already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; keep this section tool-focused, not concept-focused.
- **Slack** and **Teams** are common workplace tools; include only if collaboration stack is important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform depth and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers to show level of use: **administration, campaign deployment, segmentation, journey building, newsletter operations**
- Consider a fuller line such as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign deployment, audience segmentation, automated journeys, newsletter operations)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent work experience.
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider listing the others only if used meaningfully; otherwise this can read broader than the experience supports.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo work bullets. Tighten it to emphasize methods and business use, not just another software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Experimentation & Reporting**
- Replace with a more differentiated line such as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • Dashboard development • SEO analysis**
- Drop **A/B testing** unless you can support it with a concrete example elsewhere; if valid, use **Experiment design** instead for a more senior framing.
- Keep the list ordered by strategic weight/recent relevance: analytics stack first, then reporting/optimization capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with Looker Studio/Power BI; “Dashboard development” is stronger but still somewhat redundant.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, since leadership, governance, and scaled operations are already covered in newer entries.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-build impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Replace vague phrases like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with specifics such as “standardized publishing workflows,” “expanded in-house production capacity,” or “reduced reliance on vendors,” if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format.
- Avoid repeating team leadership/governance themes already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize cross-functional coordination and the launch outcome rather than broad content support.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy teams; translated project work into digital and multimedia content for member communications.”
- Add the standout achievement more directly: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, quantify scope: number of projects supported, podcast episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Remove vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” and “organizational programs”; use specific nouns such as policy teams, member communications, research initiatives, or multimedia assets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia language already covered in later NACo roles; keep this entry focused on research/program support and the podcast launch.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent leadership appears in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mixed capabilities section than “tools.” It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in Core Competencies and work experience.
